title: Risotto al Radicchio di Treviso
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A striking magenta-tinted risotto built on Treviso's prized bitter red chicory, its pleasant bitterness balanced by butter, Parmigiano, and a splash of red wine.
longDesc: Radicchio di Treviso is a specifically prized variety of chicory from the Veneto, its elegant elongated leaves and pleasantly bitter edge softening as it cooks into the risotto, staining the rice a beautiful deep red.
ingredients: 320 g (1½ cups) Carnaroli or Vialone Nano rice
1.2 L (5 cups) hot vegetable or chicken stock
steps: Keep the stock warm in a saucepan over low heat throughout cooking.
Melt half the butter with the olive oil in a wide pan and sauté the onion until soft.
Add most of the sliced radicchio, reserving a little for garnish, and cook for a few minutes until wilted.
Add the rice and toast, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.
Begin adding the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, for about 18 minutes until the rice is creamy with a slight bite.
Remove from the heat and beat in the remaining butter and Parmigiano vigorously.
Fold in the reserved raw radicchio for a fresh, slightly crunchy finish, and serve immediately.
chefTips: Reserving a little raw radicchio to fold in at the end adds welcome texture and fresh bitterness against the creamy rice.
The wine's acidity helps balance radicchio's natural bitterness -- don't skip it.
The final vigorous beating in of butter and cheese (mantecatura) is what gives good risotto its glossy, wave-like consistency.
commonMistakes: Adding all the radicchio at the start, losing the fresh, slightly crunchy contrast a final raw addition provides.
Adding the stock all at once instead of gradually, preventing the rice from releasing its starch properly.
Overcooking the rice until it loses all bite.
servedWith: A dry red wine from Veneto
storage: Best eaten immediately; risotto does not hold or reheat particularly well.
reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of stock, stirring constantly.
healthBenefits: Radicchio provides fiber and antioxidant compounds.
culturalNote: Radicchio di Treviso is a prized, protected vegetable of the Veneto, and this risotto is one of the most celebrated ways the region showcases its distinctive bitter flavor.
